root_cause.text: The code at fib6_add_rt2node() accesses `iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family` without first verifying that `iter->nh` is NULL, leading to an out-of-bounds read when the route was created with RTA_NH_ID (using a nexthop object) because such routes lack the trailing `fib6_nh` structure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `(iter->nh || ...)` to short-circuit the check if `iter->nh` is set; the CVE description explicitly states "When IPv6 route is created with RTA_NH_ID, struct fib6_info does not have the trailing struct fib6_nh." The KASAN report points to line 1142 in fib6_add_rt2node where the OOB read occurs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix route flag clearing logic to also handle routes using nexthop objects, not just those with direct nexthop gateway.
intent_record.what: Modified the condition in an if statement inside fib6_add_rt2node to include a check for iter->nh (nexthop object) in addition to the existing check for !iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family.
intent_record.how: Previously, flags RTF_ADDRCONF and RTF_PREFIX_RT were cleared only when the route had no gateway. Now, they are also cleared when the route uses a nexthop object (iter->nh), regardless of gateway presence.

grouping_result.intent: Fix route flag clearing logic to also handle routes using nexthop objects, not just those with direct nexthop gateway.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the handling of routes using nexthop objects, which is the core scenario leading to the out-of-bounds read vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This statement accesses iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family without checking if iter->nh is NULL, causing an out-of-bounds read on routes created with RTA_NH_ID that lack the fib6_nh structure.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement accesses iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family without first checking if iter->nh is NULL. For routes created with RTA_NH_ID (using a nexthop object), iter->nh is non-NULL and iter->fib6_nh is not part of the structure, leading to an out-of-bounds read.
